belief: Because of grace, my choices don’t matter.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that because of grace your choices don’t matter, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Reacting against legalism by swinging to the other extreme. Hearing “God will forgive anyway” used to excuse sin. Wanting freedom without responsibility. Teaching that focused on grace but never on growth. Habits that are hard to change, so it feels easier to say they don’t matter.
teaches: Grace is God’s free gift, and it never depends on our performance. But grace does not make our choices meaningless. Paul asked, “Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase? Certainly not!” The grace of God teaches us to say no to ungodliness and to live upright lives. We are called to freedom, but not to use it for the flesh; rather, to serve one another in love. Grace saves us and also changes us.
self_statements: God will forgive me anyway, so it doesn’t matter.
Grace means I don’t have to change.
My choices don’t affect my relationship with God.
I can live however I want.
errors: Believing you must choose between grace and obedience.
Downplaying the real harm sin causes.
Using grace as an excuse for choices you know are wrong.
Overlooking Scripture’s teaching that grace trains us to live well.
questions: How did Paul answer, “Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?”
What does the grace of God teach us, according to Titus 2:12?
What is freedom in Christ for, according to Galatians 5:13?
Do my choices affect me and the people I love?
Is grace something to presume on or something to respond to?
What does Ephesians 2:10 say I was created for?
What choice do I need to take more seriously?
truth: Grace is free, but my choices still matter. God’s grace saves me and also teaches me to say no to ungodliness and live a godly life. I am free in Christ, not to indulge the flesh but to serve others in love. My choices affect me, others, and my closeness with God, and grace gives me power to choose well.
hw_questions: How did Paul answer the question about sin and grace?
What does God’s grace teach me?
Am I presuming on grace or responding to it?
What was I created to do?
hw_truths: Grace is free, and my choices still matter.
God’s grace teaches me to live a godly life.
I am free to serve others in love.
Sin is not my master; I am under grace.
I was created for good works.
Grace gives me power to choose well.
log: Each day, write one choice I made because of God’s grace at work in me.
name_example: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to Sarah. It instructs her to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live a sensible, upright, and godly life in the present age.
actions: Identify one choice you’ve been excusing with grace,
and take one step to change it this week.
and write what it says about grace and the new life.
Ask a trusted believer to hold you accountable
Do one act of love for someone
as a way of using your freedom well.
prayer: Father, thank You for Your free grace. Help me reject the lie that because of grace my choices don’t matter. Let Your grace train me to say no to ungodliness and to live for You. Use my freedom to serve others in love. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
